strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with cloned buffers
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all_reduce calls with explicit buffer cloning and element-wise scale/unscale operations between stages, matching the reference implementation. Total 8 all_reduce dispatches with full W*S payload each. Trades dispatch count for implementation simplicity with no fusion or overlapping.

strategies.name: Fused local-ops between all-reduces
strategies.desc: Same 8 all_reduce dispatches but fuses all local scale/unscale operations into single kernels per stage, eliminating intermediate clone() calls by using in-place operations where safe. Reduces memory bandwidth by ~3x per stage through kernel fusion while maintaining the same collective communication pattern.

strategies.name: Pre-computed scale tensor broadcast
strategies.desc: Pre-allocates and broadcasts a (W, S) scale tensor containing all a[r] values, then uses batched element-wise operations with views to apply scales across all shards simultaneously. Still 8 all_reduce dispatches but replaces W loops with vectorized tensor operations, reducing CPU overhead and enabling better compiler optimization.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter then all-gather chain
strategies.desc: Transforms each all_reduce into a reduce_scatter followed by local scaling then all_gather, exploiting the per-shard structure. Doubles collective count to 16 dispatches but reduces per-dispatch payload from W*S to S for reduce_scatter and enables pipelining opportunities. Benefits from smaller message sizes at world_size=224.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level reduction with node-local aggregation
strategies.desc:
Exploits multi-node topology by performing intra-node all_reduce (lower latency) followed by inter-node all_reduce at each stage, leveraging num_nodes parameter. Maintains 8 logical stages but splits each into 2 collectives (16 total dispatches), optimizing for network topology at the cost of additional coordination overhead.
